```{=html}
<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 8 <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Integrals</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">8.2</span> Integration on Manifolds</h1></header>
<p>Let <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}^\uparrow)\)</span> be an oriented manifold with a volume form <span class="math inline">\(\Omega\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X}) \in \mathcal{A}^\uparrow\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>, and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{U}\)</span> the open region over which <span class="math inline">\(f\)</span> is to be integrated, with closure <span class="math inline">\(\overline{\mathcal{D}}\)</span> compact and contained in <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span><sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7" aria-label="Footnote 7">7</a></sup>. The indicator function <span class="math inline">\(\iota\)</span> of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{D}\)</span> cuts <span class="math inline">\(f\)</span> off outside the region: <span class="math inline">\(\iota f\)</span> equals <span class="math inline">\(f\)</span> on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{D}\)</span> and vanishes outside it. The <strong>integral of <span class="math inline">\(f\)</span> over <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{D}\)</span></strong> is <span class="math display" id="eq_integral_chart">\begin{equation}
    \begin{split}
        \int_\mathcal{D} \Omega f
        &amp;\coloneqq \int_{\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{U})} d^d\alpha \, \big( \omega_\mathscr{X} \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) \, \big( (\iota f) \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) \\
        &amp;\overset{\substack{\iota \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \, = \, 1 \text{ on } \mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D}) \\ \text{and } 0 \text{ outside}}}{=}
        \int_{\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D})} d^d\alpha \, \big( \omega_\mathscr{X} \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) \, \big( f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) ,
    \end{split} \tag{8.3}
\end{equation}</span> an ordinary integral over the open set <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D}) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d\)</span>, which is bounded since <span class="math inline">\(\overline{\mathcal{D}}\)</span> is compact, see Figure <a class="dg-xref" href="index.html#fig_integration_charts" data-kind="figure" data-label="fig_integration_charts">8.1</a>.</p>
<p>This definition does not depend on the chart. Let <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y}) \in \mathcal{A}^\uparrow\)</span> be a second chart with <span class="math inline">\(\overline{\mathcal{D}} \subseteq \mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V}\)</span>, so that <span class="math inline">\(\int_\mathcal{D} \Omega f\)</span> can be computed in either. The chart transition map <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛖ}_{\mathcal{V}\mathcal{U}} = \mathscr{X} \circ \mathscr{Y}^{-1}\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\alpha = \textrm{\runic ᛖ}_{\mathcal{V}\mathcal{U}}(\beta)\)</span>, maps <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{Y}(\mathcal{D})\)</span> onto <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D})\)</span>, since <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{X}\big( \mathscr{Y}^{-1}( \mathscr{Y}(\mathcal{D}) ) \big) = \mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D})\)</span>, and <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
    \int_\mathcal{D} \Omega f =
    &amp;\int_{\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{D})} d^d\alpha \, \big( \omega_\mathscr{X} \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) \, \big( f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha)
    \xlongrightarrow[d^d\alpha \, = \, d^d\beta \, |\det ( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} )(\beta)|]{\text{change of variables}} ... \\
    ... =
    &amp;\int_{\mathscr{Y}(\mathcal{D})} d^d\beta \, \Big| \det \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)(\beta) \Big| \,
    \big( \omega_\mathscr{X} \circ \underbrace{\mathscr{X}^{-1} \circ \textrm{\runic ᛖ}_{\mathcal{V}\mathcal{U}}}_{\mathscr{Y}^{-1}} \big)(\beta) \,
    \big( f \circ \underbrace{\mathscr{X}^{-1} \circ \textrm{\runic ᛖ}_{\mathcal{V}\mathcal{U}}}_{\mathscr{Y}^{-1}} \big)(\beta)
    \xlongrightarrow[\text{at } p \, = \, \mathscr{Y}^{-1}(\beta)]{(8.1)} ... \\
    ... =
    &amp;\int_{\mathscr{Y}(\mathcal{D})} d^d\beta \,
    \underbrace{\frac{\big| \det \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)(\beta) \big|}{\det \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)(\beta)}}_{= \, +1 \text{ in } \mathcal{A}^\uparrow} \,
    \big( \omega_\mathscr{Y} \circ \mathscr{Y}^{-1} \big)(\beta) \, \big( f \circ \mathscr{Y}^{-1} \big)(\beta) ,
\end{align*}</span> which is (<a class="dg-xref" href="#eq_integral_chart" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_integral_chart">8.3</a>) in the chart <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\)</span>. The absolute value produced by the change of variables is cancelled by the determinant carried by <span class="math inline">\(\omega_\mathscr{X}\)</span> only up to its sign, and the orientation makes this sign <span class="math inline">\(+1\)</span>.</p>
```

## `<span class="dg-secnum">8.2.1</span> Integral over the Whole Manifold`{=html} {#subsection_Integral_Whole_Manifold}

```{=html}
<p>A function that does not vanish outside a single chart domain is first cut into pieces that do. With <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} f \coloneqq \overline{\{ p \in \mathcal{M} \mid f(p) \neq 0 \}}\)</span> the <strong>support</strong> of <span class="math inline">\(f\)</span>, outside which <span class="math inline">\(f\)</span> vanishes, and <span class="math inline">\(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}_{a \in A}\)</span> an open cover of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>, a <strong>partition of unity</strong> subordinate to it is a family of smooth functions <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n : \mathcal{M} \to [0, 1]\)</span> such that</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p><em>subordinate:</em> each <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n\)</span> is contained in some <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}_a\)</span>;</p></li>
<li><p><em>locally finite:</em> every point has a neighbourhood that meets only finitely many <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n\)</span>;</p></li>
<li><p><em>sums to one:</em> <span class="math inline">\(\sum_n \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n(p) = 1\)</span> for all <span class="math inline">\(p \in \mathcal{M}\)</span>, a finite sum at every <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> by 2.</p></li>
</ol>
<p>Multiplying by <span class="math inline">\(1 = \sum_n \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n\)</span> splits any <span class="math inline">\(f\)</span> into the pieces <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n f\)</span>, each vanishing outside a single <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}_a\)</span>.</p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p>Let <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}^\uparrow)\)</span> be an oriented manifold with a volume form <span class="math inline">\(\Omega\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} f\)</span> compact, and <span class="math inline">\(\{ \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \}\)</span> a partition of unity subordinate to the cover of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span> by the chart domains of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{A}^\uparrow\)</span>, with <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n\)</span> for a chart <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{U}_n, \mathscr{X}_n) \in \mathcal{A}^\uparrow\)</span><sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-8" id="fnref-8" aria-label="Footnote 8">8</a></sup>. The <strong>integral of <span class="math inline">\(f\)</span> over <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span></strong> is <span class="math display" id="eq_integral_manifold">\begin{equation}
    \int_\mathcal{M} \Omega f \coloneqq \sum_n \int_{\mathcal{U}_n} \Omega \, \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n f . \tag{8.4}
\end{equation}</span> Each term is defined by (<a class="dg-xref" href="#eq_integral_chart" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_integral_chart">8.3</a>), with <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{D}\)</span> any open set containing <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \cap \operatorname{supp} f\)</span> with closure compact and contained in <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}_n\)</span>: this set is compact, as a closed subset of the compact <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} f\)</span>, so such <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{D}\)</span> exist, and <span class="math inline">\(\iota \, \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n f = \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n f\)</span> makes the value independent of the choice. Only finitely many terms are non-zero, since the compact <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} f\)</span> is covered by finitely many of the neighbourhoods of item 2. The result does not depend on the partition of unity chosen.</p>
<div class="dg-footnotes"><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-7"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-7" aria-label="Back to the text">7</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p>The closure <span class="math inline">\(\overline{\mathcal{D}}\)</span> is <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{D}\)</span> together with its boundary points. Its compactness makes the integral  finite, and its containment in <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span> makes it an ordinary integral over a bounded region of <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{X}(\mathcal{U})\)</span>.  Without these conditions the integral may diverge (Appendix <a class="dg-xref" href="../proofs-and-additional-material/support-integrals.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_appendix_support_integrals">B.19</a>).</p></div></div><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-8"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-8" aria-label="Back to the text">8</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p>Such a partition of unity exists because <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span> is Hausdorff and second countable  (Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../topological-manifolds/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Topological_Manifolds">3</a>). The cover by all chart domains of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{A}^\uparrow\)</span> is not locally finite, since  infinitely many charts contain each point, but these two properties allow it to be refined to a cover in which every  point has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many of its sets, and the partition of unity is built on this  refinement (Appendix <a class="dg-xref" href="../proofs-and-additional-material/partitions-of-unity.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_appendix_partitions_of_unity">B.20</a>).</p></div></div></div>

```
